items.headline: US-China talks broaden to AI, trade and critical minerals
items.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng are set to open talks covering AI safeguards, trade and critical minerals ahead of a Trump-Xi summit, with the trade truce and rare-earth supply among unresolved issues.
items.whyItMatters: Critical minerals and AI controls are now being negotiated alongside tariffs, directly linking semiconductor supply chains to geopolitical risk.

items.headline: China's CXMT moves fifth-generation memory platform into mass production
items.summary: Chinese DRAM producer CXMT says its fifth-generation memory platform has entered mass production, using advanced patterning to improve density, cost and power efficiency while introducing higher-capacity LPDDR5X products.
items.whyItMatters: This is a tangible localization milestone that can increase long-run competitive pressure on incumbent memory suppliers and reduce China's dependence on foreign semiconductor technology.

items.headline: Gulf equities absorb renewed Saudi security risk
items.summary: Saudi and other Gulf equity markets weakened after Houthis claimed missile and drone attacks on Riyadh. Saudi Arabia's main index closed modestly lower while Qatar fell more sharply; diplomatic efforts involving China and Iran remain active.
items.whyItMatters: The market reaction confirms that physical-security risk remains relevant even as crude logistics improve.
